meta.promptText: Which vitamin C serum should I buy for dark spots and dull skin in India?

response.text:
For **dark spots + dull skin**, I’d start with a **10% vitamin C serum** rather than jumping straight to 15–20%. Stable derivatives such as **3-O-ethyl ascorbic acid** are a practical choice in India because they’re generally more stable and less irritating than high-strength pure L-ascorbic acid. [phdbeauty.com](https://phdbeauty.com/blogs/general-advice/best-vitamin-c-serum-india-2026?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

### My picks

### [Asaya 15% Vitamin C + E & Ferulic Acid Serum]()

### [The Derma Co 15% Vitamin C Face Serum]()
*₹703*

**🥇 Best overall: Minimalist 10% Vitamin C**  
A good starting point for pigmentation and dullness, particularly if you haven't used vitamin C before. It uses a stable vitamin C derivative and is positioned for dark spots/uneven tone. [www.mrpuku.com](https://www.mrpuku.com/2026/02/Vitamin-C-Serum.html?m=1&utm_source=chatgpt.com)

**🥈 If you've used vitamin C before: Plum 15%**  
A stronger option if your skin tolerates actives well and your main goal is more noticeable brightening/spot fading.

**🥉 If you want a stronger antioxidant formula: Asaya 15% Vitamin C + E + Ferulic Acid**  
Vitamin E and ferulic acid are useful companions to vitamin C, and this is a reasonable step-up option.

### How I'd use it
**Morning:** cleanser → 2–3 drops vitamin C → moisturizer → **SPF 50 sunscreen**.

Sunscreen is particularly important for dark spots; otherwise UV exposure can keep stimulating pigmentation and undermine your progress. Consistent treatment generally takes **several weeks to a few months**, rather than days. sources.snippet:
This article from Who What Wear UK provides a comprehensive guide to the best skincare products for treating hyperpigmentation, featuring insights from dermatologists and skin experts. Hyperpigmentation, a common skin concern caused by excess melanin, can result from sun exposure, hormonal changes (such as pregnancy-related melasma), inflammation, or acne scarring. The guide emphasizes that the cause of pigmentation determines the best treatment and underlines the importance of daily SPF use as the most critical step in both prevention and treatment.

Recommended ingredients include vitamin C, niacinamide, azelaic acid, tranexamic acid, and retinoids, which can be found in both over-the-counter and prescription products. Experts caution that results typically take 6 to 12 weeks, or even months, and consistency in skincare is essential.

The article highlights 13 carefully selected products, spanning cleansers, serums, moisturizers, and SPFs. Notable mentions include La Roche-Posay Mela B3 Cleanser, Eucerin Pigment Control SPF50+, The Ordinary Azelaic Acid 10%, and Murad Rapid Dark Spot Correcting Serum. Each product is chosen based on expert input, performance, ingredient quality, and user reviews, providing practical options for anyone tackling dark spots and uneven skin tone.
